conviction_note: The two measurements are close but get there differently. The findings sum to +0.3: a small one-off tariff-refund upside and some organic momentum, against a softer Getinge demand read and cost pressure. The scaled number is (2*0.51-1)*5.0 = +0.1, because a refund beat is a one-off that this name and H&M have both sold, 7 of Arjo's last 8 report days fell (including Q2 2026, a 7% EBIT beat), and the 3-5% organic guide is unlikely to change before the new targets due in Q1 2027.

findings.finding: Arjo's Q2 report says a further IEEPA refund claim of a little over SEK 30M was pending; refunds are booked in COGS, so inside adjusted EBIT. On 2026-10-21 Getinge, a Swedish medtech exporter going through the same US refund process, booked SEK 45M of tariff refunds in its Q3. That makes it likely Arjo's ~30M lands in Q3: about +15% on a 193 bar, which only some analysts (SB1 at 210) model.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: adj. EBIT 211 against 197 consensus (+7.1%), with the 22M refund inside it. Ex-refund about 189, a miss. The stock fell 2.2% on the day (Finwire table). H&M's refund-made beat was also sold (LESSONS).
findings.original_quote: Koncernen har erhållit en initial återbetalning gällande amerikanska tariffer under International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) om cirka 22 Mkr, som har reducerat kostnaden för sålda varor i kvartalet. Ytterligare krav om återbetalning om drygt 30 Mkr är fortfarande under behandling. [The Group received an initial refund of ~SEK 22M of IEEPA tariffs, which reduced cost of goods sold in the quarter. A further refund claim of a little over SEK 30M is still being processed.]  Getinge Q3: 'positivt påverkad av tullåterbetalningar om 45 Mkr' [positively affected by tariff refunds of SEK 45M]
findings.why_not_priced: The Modular consensus of 193 sits 17 MSEK below SB1's 210, which explicitly includes refunded tariffs. If every analyst modelled the refund, the bar would be near 210. Getinge's Q3 confirmed refunds are flowing this quarter, Getinge rose 2.8% on 10-21, and Arjo closed -0.07% the same day, so no read-across was priced. The size is held small because the money is a one-off, the claim was disclosed in July, and the last refund-aided beat was sold.

findings.finding: Organic momentum runs ahead of the Q3 bar: Q2 organic was 4.7% against 3.3% consensus and H1 4.2%, with the CEO citing high demand (ceiling lifts, Maxi Move 5, beds, service, record ReNu), while Q3 consensus is 3.19% against a 3.8% Q3 2025 comparison.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 organic beat 4.7% vs 3.3%, stock -2.2% on the day and +3.8% the next session (tape). Growth beats have not been rewarded on the report day.
findings.original_quote: Den organiska tillväxten uppgick till 4,7 procent, mot väntade 3,3 procent. [Organic growth was 4.7%, against an expected 3.3%.]
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus organic of 3.19% for Q3 is below the H1 run-rate of 4.2% and below the middle of the guide. If the market expected momentum to carry, the bar would sit near 4%. This is partly inference: Q3 is seasonally slower and the comparison is tougher than Q2's 3.0%.
findings.independence: The company's own outlook implies H2 within 3-5% (Q2 report): https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bc6ade6b0b5e1b6cb1dd82280ab564150&lang=en&src=listed (same issuer, so not independent)

findings.finding: Getinge's Q3 shows hospital-equipment demand slowing: organic sales growth fell to 2.1% (Q2 4.6%) and organic order intake to 2.6% (Q2 6.2%), a softer read for Arjo's capital-goods mix.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Arjo-specific history on peer read-through; Arjo was flat (-0.07%) on Getinge's report day.
findings.why_not_priced: Arjo did not move on 10-21, either way. This is a peer proxy, not an Arjo number. Getinge's slowdown is partly a 9.5% comparison and is concentrated in Life Science/pharma capex, which Arjo does not have, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Gross-margin and cost pressure continued into H2: Q2 gross margin was 42.1% (43.4%) on mix, materials and transport costs plus non-recurring problems with a new transportation management system. The CEO called the cost environment 'fortsatt utmanande', and Pareto has argued margin expectations are too optimistic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (-10.5%) and Q3 2024 (-15.7%) were the large negative report days in the Finwire table. Q2 2026's gross-margin decline came with a -2.2% day despite the EBIT beat.
findings.original_quote: Sammantaget levererar vi ett stabilt kvartal, trots ett fortsatt utmanande kostnadsläge i vår omvärld [Overall we deliver a stable quarter, despite a continued challenging cost environment]
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is the known bear case and Pareto has said it publicly. It stays as a small negative because Q3 2025's gross margin (41.1%) is a low base, and a further y/y decline would make the refund beat look low quality.

findings.finding: Q3 cash flow should rebound: Q2 working capital was -122 MSEK because heavy late-quarter sales raised receivables, which normally unwind in Q3. Q3 2025 cash conversion was 105%, and Getinge reported free cash flow of 1,302 (793) for the same quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction on this line for Arjo.
findings.why_not_priced: Cash flow is not in the Modular bar, which covers sales, organic growth, EBITDA and EBIT only. With net debt/EBITDA at 2.4 and a 370 MSEK programme to fund, a strong conversion figure would answer SB1's stated demand for 'starkare kassaflöde'. Small, because it is seasonal and expected.
